questions.question: With C, how should pip find cli-extended, given that the bare name on PyPI is a dependency-confusion risk?

options.label: GH Releases + --no-index (Recommended)
options.description: Release cli-extended like every other tool (GitHub Release plus a `cli-extended-latest/latest.json` pointer). Every installer (dstdns env-setup, cmru installer `[[installer.wheels]]`, mdt, devcontainer deploy) installs it first, verifies its sha256, and installs tool wheels with `--no-index --find-links <cache>`, so PyPI is never consulted. Filed as cmru and dstdns backlog items.

options.label: Also claim PyPI name
options.description: Same as the first option, but also publish cli-extended (or a placeholder) to PyPI so nobody else can take the name. Outward-facing: the package becomes public on PyPI.

options.label: Distinctive name
options.description: Rename the distribution to something like `vbpub-cli-extended` and keep the import name `cli_extended`. This lowers the collision odds but doesn't remove the risk; still pair it with `--no-index`.

questions.question: The Netcup scripts run from a checkout, and debian-install-v2 copies itself onto fresh remote Debian hosts. Under C, how do they get cli-extended?

options.label: Venv + pinned wheel (Recommended)
options.description: Netcup scripts import from the installed cli-extended (the devcontainer venv); their gate lanes keep PYTHONPATH pointed at the worktree source, so the revision under test is the one tested. debian-install-v2's remote bootstrap stops copying a git subtree. Instead it downloads the released, pure-Python cli-extended wheel by sha256 from its release manifest and puts the `.whl` on `sys.path` (zipimport), so the remote needs no pip.

options.label: Remote pip install
options.description: Same for Netcup, but debian-install-v2 creates a venv on the remote host and pip-installs the wheel. More standard; needs python3-venv on the target.
